qualifying_findings.title: Royal MCP WordPress preview-token scope bypass
qualifying_findings.security_fact: Royal MCP before 1.5.7 does not bind a preview-link token to one preview. A holder of a valid token is authenticated as its owner across the REST API; the default configuration can turn that into administrator-level site takeover.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Royal MCP WordPress plugin before 1.5.7; preview-link token to REST-API authorization boundary.
qualifying_findings.mitigation_or_patch: Upgrade to 1.5.7 or later and invalidate or rotate exposed preview tokens.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: An MCP-branded integration must scope bearer-like preview credentials to the exact resource and action they authorize, rather than trusting possession across an administrative API.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: ai-wiki owns broad Royal MCP and WordPress catalog context; this repository retains the token-scope authorization failure.
qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High for publication timing, vulnerable version, and authorization impact; primary maintainer advisory was not listed in the CVE record.
follow_up_actions: Verify the WPScan entry and maintainer changelog for exact remediation behavior during ingest.

qualifying_findings.title: Flexible GraphRAG FalkorDB ingestion Cypher injection
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: CVE Program record with maintainer GitHub advisory, fix commit, and release reference
qualifying_findings.security_fact: Flexible GraphRAG 0.6.0 through before 0.8.2 escapes quotes before backslashes then interpolates extraction values into FalkorDB Cypher. Attacker-influenced ingested content can make the extraction model produce values that alter or delete graph data and may disclose graph data when results reach a user or model.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Flexible GraphRAG 0.6.0 to before 0.8.2 when GRAPH_BACKEND=langchain and GRAPH_DB=falkordb; document ingestion to graph-query boundary. LlamaIndex FalkorDB is not affected.
qualifying_findings.mitigation_or_patch: Upgrade to 0.8.2 or later; parameterize data values and treat model-extracted graph fields as untrusted input.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: RAG ingestion can translate untrusted documents into state-changing database commands; escaping policy must survive model-mediated extraction and backend query construction.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: ai-wiki owns broad Flexible GraphRAG and RAG framework context; this repository owns the untrusted-ingestion and graph-integrity control boundary.
qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High; the CVE record supplies exact scope, non-affected alternative, fixed version, and maintainer references.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, cross-check the maintainer advisory and fixed commit before deriving secure-query implementation guidance.

qualifying_findings.title: Agent Zero Web UI stored XSS in agent chat and uploads
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: CVE Program record with project release and CISA CSAF reference
qualifying_findings.security_fact: Agent Zero Web UI before 1.15 insufficiently sanitizes user-supplied chat-message and file-upload content. Rendering that content runs injected JavaScript in an authenticated Agent Zero session.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Agent Zero Web UI before 1.15; user content to authenticated agent-console rendering boundary.
qualifying_findings.mitigation_or_patch: Upgrade to 1.15 or later and preserve output encoding and content-isolation controls for rendered agent inputs and tool artifacts.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Agent interfaces often render model, tool, and uploaded content alongside privileged controls; stored XSS can convert untrusted agent inputs into session-level authority.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: ai-wiki owns broad Agent Zero context; this repository retains the privileged agent-console content-rendering security finding.
qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High for timing, version, and mechanism from the CVE record; review the project release notes for remediation specifics during ingest.
follow_up_actions: Verify whether v1.15 includes additional session invalidation or CSP changes before synthesis.

qualifying_findings.title: LiteLLM cryptographic-context reuse enables forged administrator tokens
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: CVE Program record with maintainer GitHub advisory, patch commits, and fixed releases
qualifying_findings.security_fact: LiteLLM 1.87.0 through before 1.100.4, 1.101.3, 1.102.2, 1.103.1, and 1.104.0-rc.2 uses one cryptographic context for at-rest secrets and session tokens. An authenticated internal user can craft API-key metadata into a forged encrypted administrator credential, replay it as a bearer token, and gain proxy-administrator access and arbitrary MCP stdio commands.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: LiteLLM 1.87.0 through affected release lines; at-rest secret encryption to session-token identity boundary. 1.87.0 through 1.90.x also require EXPERIMENTAL_UI_LOGIN; later affected versions are default-exploitable.
qualifying_findings.mitigation_or_patch: Upgrade to 1.100.4, 1.101.3, 1.102.2, 1.103.1, or 1.104.0-rc.2 as applicable; rotate affected secrets and tokens according to maintainer guidance.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: AI gateways commonly broker provider credentials and MCP authority; cryptographic domain separation is required so encrypted metadata cannot become an administrative identity.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: ai-wiki owns broad LiteLLM and AI-gateway context; this repository retains identity forgery, credential-domain separation, and MCP authority implications.
qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High; the CVE record includes exact affected/fixed lines, exploit preconditions, and maintainer advisory references.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, confirm the maintainer rotation and deployment-remediation steps before turning them into operating guidance.

qualifying_findings.title: Amazon Strands A2A cross-tenant conversation-state injection
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: CVE Program record with AWS security bulletin, maintainer GitHub advisory, and package-release references
qualifying_findings.security_fact: The A2A server in Amazon Strands Agents SDK for Python before 1.43.0 and TypeScript before 1.5.0 fails to isolate conversation state by caller. An authenticated remote user can read another tenant's history and add persistent instructions affecting later callers by using a different context_id.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: strands-agents Python before 1.43.0 and @strands-agents/sdk TypeScript before 1.5.0; A2A context_id to caller/tenant authorization boundary.
qualifying_findings.mitigation_or_patch: Upgrade to strands-agents 1.43.0 or @strands-agents/sdk 1.5.0 or later; bind conversation state to authenticated principal and tenant server-side.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Cross-tenant agent memory can leak confidential conversation state and persist attacker instructions into another user's future model execution.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: ai-wiki owns broad Strands Agents context; this repository retains the distinct cross-tenant conversation-state authorization and persistent-instruction boundary. Existing local Strands consent-bypass coverage is related but not duplicative.
qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High; the CVE record names both package ecosystems, affected versions, impact, and fixed versions.
follow_up_actions: Compare with the existing Strands nested-tool consent-bypass leaf during ingest, but keep the state-isolation issue as a separate boundary.

qualifying_findings.title: OpenAI frontier-AI cyber-defender governance blueprint
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: Official provider security and global-affairs publication
qualifying_findings.security_fact: OpenAI published a security-governance blueprint proposing clearer responsibilities for securing frontier models and agents, dangerous-behavior detection, reliable shutdown controls, independent technical assessment, consistent incident reporting, and coordinated response and recovery.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Frontier-model and agent operational governance; no software version or patch applies.
qualifying_findings.mitigation_or_patch: This is a proposed governance and assurance control set, not a vulnerability remediation or binding regulation.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: It is an in-window, concrete provider security-control and assurance proposal that informs operational expectations for monitoring, shutdown, evaluation, incident evidence, and recovery.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: ai-wiki owns broad OpenAI product and organization coverage; this repository retains only the AI-security governance, monitoring, shutdown, evaluation, and incident-response implication.
qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High that the official publication makes these proposals; it should not be represented as enacted regulation or independently verified implementation.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, distinguish the blueprint's proposals from mandatory standards and from product-specific controls.
